thread.title: Honeywell Aerospace signs agreement with Department of War to boost defense production
thread.title_full: Honeywell Aerospace signs agreement with Department of War to boost defense production

author: T. R. Burke
title: Honeywell Aerospace signs agreement with Department of War to boost defense production
text:
Honeywell announced on March 25 that it has signed a supplier framework agreement with the U.S. Department of War to increase the production of critical defense technologies. The agreement includes a $500 million multi-year investment aimed at upgrading Honeywell’s production capacity.
This move marks Honeywell Aerospace as one of the first Tier 1 suppliers to enter into such an agreement with the Department of War, reflecting its commitment to meeting national defense needs.
“Honeywell Aerospace is proud to embrace the challenge and meet this urgent need,” said Jim Currier, president and CEO of Honeywell Aerospace. “Our commercial operating system enables us to invest in advanced technologies and manufacture at scale and speed, delivering a substantial and enduring benefit to the customer and taxpayers.”
Under this new arrangement, Honeywell Aerospace will ramp up its production efforts for various critical technologies needed by American and allied forces. The company’s aerospace division produces engines, cockpit electronics, wireless connectivity solutions, thermal systems, power units, actuation systems, and other hardware for commercial, defense, space aircrafts as well as terrestrial systems.
Honeywell operates globally across multiple industries using its proprietary Accelerator operating system and Forge platform. The company aims to provide solutions for aerospace technology as well as building automation and industrial processes.
